Given the supply voltage $v(t) = 141.4 \sin(377t)\text{ V}$, the RMS voltage is $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{141.4}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 100\text{ V}$ and angular frequency $\omega = 377\text{ rad/s}$.

1. **Calculate impedances:**
   * Inductor $L_1 = 1\text{ H}$: $X_{L1} = \omega L_1 = 377 \times 1 = 377\text{ }\Omega$
   * Capacitor $C = 10\text{ }\mu\text{F}$: $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{377 \times 10 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 265.25\text{ }\Omega$
   * Inductor $L_2 = 2.35\text{ H}$: $X_{L2} = \omega L_2 = 377 \times 2.35 \approx 885.95\text{ }\Omega$

2. **Parallel combination impedance ($Z_p$):**
   $Z_p = \frac{(-j X_C)(j X_{L2})}{j(X_{L2} - X_C)} = \frac{(-j 265.25)(j 885.95)}{j(885.95 - 265.25)} = \frac{234914.86}{j 620.7} = -j 378.46\text{ }\Omega$
   *(Wait, let's re-verify the parallel branch: $C$ and $L_2$ are in parallel, so $Z_p = \frac{-j X_C \cdot j X_{L2}}{j(X_{L2}-X_C)} = \frac{X_C X_{L2}}{X_{L2}-X_C} = \frac{265.25 \times 885.95}{885.95 - 265.25} = \frac{234914.86}{620.7} = +378.46\text{ }\Omega$ (inductive)*
   Let's use complex arithmetic correctly: $Z_p = \frac{(265.25\lfloor -90^\circ)(885.95\lfloor 90^\circ)}{885.95\lfloor 90^\circ - 265.25\lfloor -90^\circ} = +j 378.46\text{ }\Omega$.

3. **Total Equivalent Impedance ($Z_{\text{total}}$):**
   $Z_{\text{total}} = R_1 + j X_{L1} + Z_p = 100 + j377 + j378.46 = 100 + j755.46\text{ }\Omega$
   Magnitude $|Z_{\text{total}}| = \sqrt{100^2 + 755.46^2} = \sqrt{10000 + 570719.8} = \sqrt{580719.8} \approx 762.05\text{ }\Omega$.

(i) **RMS Line Current ($I_{\text{rms}}$):**
$I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}}}{|Z_{\text{total}}|} = \frac{100}{762.05} \approx 0.1312\text{ A}$

(ii) **Power Dissipated ($P$):**
$P = I_{\text{rms}}^2 R_1 = (0.1312)^2 \times 100 \approx 1.72\text{ W}$

(iii) **Power Factor (pf):**
$\text{pf} = \cos(\theta) = \frac{R_1}{|Z_{\text{total}}|} = \frac{100}{762.05} \approx 0.1312\text{ lagging}$
proTip: Always reduce series-parallel AC networks into a single equivalent complex impedance $Z = R + jX$ before finding currents and power.
